🚀 Explore 2,234 interactive 3D anatomy meshes right in your browser with React, Three.js, and a brilliantly optimized rendering pipeline!

Building immersive 3D web apps usually comes with a massive bottleneck: rendering complex datasets smoothly without tanking your frame rate. Human Atlas solves this challenge by converting the BodyParts3D adult male reference model into a high-performance 3D anatomy explorer with over 2,200 selectable meshes, 15 anatomical systems, and searchable concepts.

Here is what makes this repository a masterclass in WebGL and Three.js optimization:

⚡ High-Performance Batch Rendering: Merges geometry and utilizes per-structure GPU textures for translation, visibility, and selection to maintain responsive orbit controls without thousands of separate draw calls.

💥 Granular Selectability & Exploded Views: Dynamically separates the anatomical model into 2,234 individually selectable meshes and packs visible pieces into non-overlapping exploded layouts for desktop and mobile aspect ratios.

🔍 Comprehensive Search and Inspection: Integrates indexing for 3,432 named concepts and source identifiers, supporting structural isolation, detail reading, and optional WebMCP tool integration.

📦 Lightweight Asset Delivery: Optimizes massive medical data down to roughly 33 MB of compressed geometry using custom conversion, optimization, and compression scripts.

Whether you are building educational EdTech apps for biology and physiology, or looking to study advanced architectural patterns for managing, batching, and picking thousands of distinct 3D objects in the browser, this codebase is an absolute goldmine.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/ashemag/human-atlas

Tired of text-only prompt engineering resulting in completely hallucinated UI layouts from your AI coding agents? 

Bridge the gap between visual layout sketching and AI prompt engineering with lnkiai/m3e-canvas: an interactive browser-based canvas for Google's Material 3 Expressive design system.

The Problem:
Text prompts struggle to capture multi-screen flows, exact hierarchies, and complex UI states. Writing lengthy descriptions of layout coordinates wastes time and usually leads to messy, broken code from LLMs.

The Solution:
M3E Canvas lets you visually compose screens in seconds. Layout multi-screen flows, connect states, and apply Google's Material 3 Expressive styling, then instantly transpile your visual schema into structured prompts tailored for Claude Code, Cursor, and more.

Notable Features:
* Magnetic UI Connections: Automatically fuses close components with softening corner transitions for rapid wireframing.
* M3 Expressive Theme Engine: Controls seed-based color systems, typography, shape morphing, and motion springs directly in the browser.
* Bi-directional Multi-Screen Flow: Supports phone and desktop viewports with stateful tap/swipe transitions and interactive previews.
* Structured LLM Prompt Generation: Translates complex layout hierarchies and component notes into concise prompts targeting Android or web tech stacks.

Perfect for frontend devs, AI prompt engineers, and indie hackers leveraging vibe-coding workflows to ship faster without layout hallucinations.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/lnkiai/m3e-canvas

Stop your AI from hallucinating code and binary structures by turning deterministic tools into the final legal judge of every claim. 🛑🤖

If you are building autonomous coding agents or working with reverse-engineering workflows, you know the pain of LLM hallucinations breaking your code and poisoning context windows. 

Enter Reverify: an anti-hallucination verification engine and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that blocks language models from asserting unverified facts. Instead of blindly trusting an AI's output, Reverify forces the model to propose structural or behavioral claims that are immediately checked against ground truth using deterministic tools like parsers, disassemblers, and emulators. Only claims that successfully survive verification are accepted. 🛡️

Here is what makes it a game-changer for your workflow:

⚡ Deterministic Verification Loop: Intercepts AI hypotheses and runs them against a pure-Python RE toolkit (or optional backends like Capstone, Unicorn, Lief, and Z3), returning VERIFIED or REFUTED with concrete evidence.
📊 Information-Weighted Grounding: Weighs verified claims based on binary entropy and uniqueness (following FActScore principles), stopping the AI from passing off trivial assertions like zero padding as meaningful proof.
🔌 Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration: Out-of-the-box MCP server support lets AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI natively invoke verification tools during active sessions.
🔄 Context Rollover Mechanism: Mitigates context rot during long developer tasks by automatically handing off sessions to files and spinning up fresh ones without manual clear commands.

Whether you are gating CI/CD pipelines to fail builds when an agent proposes a hallucinated patch, or doing automated malware analysis and CTF binary reconstruction, Reverify acts as a cryptographic quality gate for production-grade LLM workflows. 🚀

Check it out on GitHub and secure your agentic workflows today:
https://github.com/2akouwu/reverify

Stop fighting raw RPC scrapers and messy API pagination just to analyze Polymarket data. 

PolyLedger packages complex Polymarket CLOB metadata and Polygon on-chain trades into a single, highly-performant DuckDB file for instant SQL analytics.

Building trading strategies or ML models on decentralized prediction markets usually means getting bogged down by data engineering bottlenecks. PolyLedger solves this by syncing Polymarket metadata and streaming Polygon OrderFilled events (both V1 and V2 generations) straight into a unified, portable DuckDB database. 

Here is why data engineers and crypto quants are adding it to their stack:

⚡ Resumable by Construction: Atomic transactions commit rows and block cursors together, allowing safe interruption and instant incremental updates without data corruption.

🔄 Dual Contract Decoding: Seamlessly handles both legacy V1 and modern V2 OrderFilled event layouts with separate streams and checkpoints.

🛡️ Fault-Tolerant Ingestion: Features robust validation using Pydantic models, exponential backoff with jitter, and a shared token-bucket rate limiter.

📊 Clean Analytical Model: Explicitly tracks maker and taker sides, converting raw amounts into clean USD sizes, shares, and execution prices without ambiguity.

Save dozens of hours of development time. Query your data immediately via SQL or dump it directly into Parquet files for use with pandas, polars, or Spark. Perfect for building historical backtesting engines or training machine learning models in your Python notebooks.

Check out the repository and start querying:
https://github.com/nahrek/polyledger

Most AI agents stop learning the second they hit production. They execute tasks, fail, and require you to manually collect traces, fine-tune offline, and redeploy. 

Enter Reef: the first open-source continual learning infrastructure built specifically for self-improving AI agents. It bridges inference, feedback loops, and version-controlled weight or harness updates into a single unified runtime. 🚀

Here is how Reef solves the post-deployment stagnation problem:

🔄 Four-Stage Learning Pipeline: Automates your complete lifecycle from live request serving (Serve) and feedback matching (Observe) to generation of updates (Grow) and validation/versioned publishing (Commit).

🔀 Dual-Surface Optimization: Supports both weight-training via Slime and SGLang, and harness optimization to evolve prompts, rules, and skills via model APIs without needing local training GPUs.

🔌 Drop-In Compatibility: Integrates seamlessly with your existing stack using standard OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints, complete with receipt headers for tracking interaction feedback.

⚡ Zero-Downtime Hot Swapping: Automatically synchronizes updated model weights or agent skill configurations to your serving runtime so production traffic experiences zero disruption during updates.

Whether you are building autonomous coding agents that self-correcting when failing unit tests or domain-specific chat agents improving via user reward scores, Reef gives your agents a continuous feedback loop.

Check it out on GitHub and star the project to support open-source AI infrastructure:
https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef
